bullets.title: AAPL: Citi survey shows brand leadership intact, AI shortening upgrade cycles to 2.1-2.7 yrs
bullets.body: Citi's survey of 4,000+ global consumers shows AAPL purchase consideration exceeds current ownership levels across all regions, supporting share gains. Smartphone upgrade cycles are compressing from 2.9-4.3 years to 2.1-2.7 years driven by AI-enabled devices and Apple Intelligence. Mac gaining share across regions; iPad remains dominant in tablets; foldable phones represent a compelling premium opportunity with strong US/UK interest.

bullets.title: META: Arke chip H1 2027, Astrid chip H2 2027 deployment confirmed; Meta One subscription launches
bullets.body: META confirmed deployment of in-house Arke GPU in H1 2027 and Astrid chip by end of 2027, validating the AVGO ASIC partnership thesis per JPM. Meta One subscription service with AI features launched today. META +0.7% on the day; GS notes investor sentiment uptick on Muse launch ahead of Meta Connect with key debate on whether product momentum is sustainable.

bullets.title: AVGO: META ASIC partnership confirmed but stock underperforming; networking complexity key
bullets.body: JPM's intraday note highlights that META shipping custom ASICs (Arke GPU H1 2027, Astrid H2 2027) confirms the AVGO partnership thesis, yet AVGO was underperforming on the day. JPM flags networking complexity as the next key variable to watch. AVGO CEO separately reiterated confidence that inference and compute demand will remain 'very strong.'

bullets.title: NVDA: In talks to anchor Anthropic IPO with up to $10B investment at ~$2T valuation
bullets.body: Anthropic's IPO is expected early November on Nasdaq (MS and GS as leads) at a ~$2T valuation with a $100B total raise; NVDA is reportedly in talks to invest up to $10B as anchor investor. Anthropic's tokenized market cap is up +523% since November 2025. Separately, NVDA CEO pushed back against AI doomer predictions at a public event today.

bullets.title: NET: Retesting/breaking ATHs; hard-to-find fundamental bears with Act IV monetization catalyst ahead
bullets.body: GS notes Cloudflare is retesting and breaking all-time highs with virtually no fundamental bears in the market. Bulls cite the near-term traffic delivery story and the medium-term 'Act IV' monetization roadmap as key catalysts. Hedgeye also lists NET as a 'signal strength long' in the AI agentic software infrastructure theme alongside TWLO, CRWD, and DT.

bullets.title: CRM: KeyBanc Sector Weight; Dreamforce bundle strategy early but partners uncertain on pricing
bullets.body: KeyBanc takeaways from CRM partner breakfast: new Core/Advanced/Max bundle embeds Slack, Agentforce, and analytics with a ~10% uplift not yet surfacing in active sales cycles. Agentforce adoption concentrated in healthcare and financial services; consumption-led model possible in 5 years but not executable today. CRM trades 21.0x CY27 P/E vs. peer avg 21.6x — KeyBanc views it as fairly valued.

bullets.title: MDB: Self-managed deployments now a double-digit growth engine; no Atlas cannibalization
bullets.body: At Piper Sandler conference, MongoDB management highlighted that self-managed deployments have accelerated for three consecutive quarters and are now expected to contribute double-digit ARR growth, with no cannibalization of Atlas. Large customers use both, and Atlas growth is running above company average. MDB is positioning its JSON-native architecture for AI agent memory layer use cases.

bullets.title: MRVL: Jefferies rates BUY with $325 PT; CEO/CFO non-deal roadshow Oct 7 NYC
bullets.body: Jefferies analyst Blayne Curtis reiterates BUY on Marvell Technology with a $325 price target. The firm is hosting a limited (15-investor) non-deal roadshow with CEO Matt Murphy, CFO Dan Durn, and IR on October 7 in NYC.

bullets.title: CIEN: Catching bid ahead of invite-only Calgary factory tour tomorrow
bullets.body: JPM notes CIEN is catching a bid in today's session ahead of an invite-only factory tour in Calgary tomorrow, where incremental guidance color is expected. No rating or PT specifics provided, but the event is seen as a near-term positive catalyst.

bullets.title: HOOD: Down 3.4% on DoJ crypto fraud charges vs employees; non-crypto revenue 80-90% of mix — oversold per Mizuho
bullets.body: Robinhood fell 3.4% after DoJ charged two employees with crypto-related trading fraud, compounding the -3% relative move from the CLARITY Act Senate cloture failure. Mizuho argues HOOD is overpenalized given that 80-90% of revenue is non-crypto related and the legal action is employee-specific, not structural.

bullets.title: DKNG/HOOD: Prediction market sports betting legality faces near-term federal court risk
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged a call on the legal status of sports bets on prediction market platforms, noting federal courts could rule soon with meaningful implications for HOOD and DKNG. States are stepping up enforcement and exploring geofencing; multiple legal cases in progress with Supreme Court potential.

bullets.title: NYT: Guggenheim upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $82 from $70 on low-double-digit digital ad growth outlook
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgraded NYT from Neutral to Buy and raised its price target to $82 from $70, citing confidence in low-double-digit digital advertising growth in coming quarters.

bullets.title: CART: Down 5.4% on Edgewater Research note flagging potential DASH-COST partnership risk
bullets.body: Instacart fell 5.4% after Edgewater Research commented on a potential DoorDash-Costco partnership that could threaten CART's grocery delivery positioning. No further PT or rating detail provided.

bullets.title: RBLX: Algorithm change benefits Adopt Me!; platform pushing 17+ audience; AI build tools rolling out
bullets.body: Jefferies expert call with Adopt Me! developer highlights that Roblox recently changed its recommendation algorithm, lifting Adopt Me! to top charts. Roblox is actively pushing to attract 17+ and older audiences and is promoting AI tools for in-experience building. Age and chat restrictions continue to create platform headwinds.

bullets.title: AMZN: Flat vs. S&P 500 over past 8 years per GS; cited as competitive threat to MELI in LatAm
bullets.body: GS notes AMZN has returned approximately the same as the S&P 500 since September 2018 — a notable underperformance framing for the stock. Separately, Hedgeye cites Amazon FBA and third-party partnerships as a legitimate competitive threat to MercadoLibre in Latin America alongside TikTok and Shopee.

bullets.title: AVGO/AMD/AMZN: Wolfe Research semis webcast covers AMD pre-quiet call and QCOM/AMZN deal
bullets.body: Wolfe Research hosted a semiconductors webcast today covering AMD's pre-quiet period call, the QCOM-AMZN deal, and an AVGO earnings recap alongside TMT conference takeaways. Slides and replay are available; no specific PT changes noted in summary.

bullets.title: DELL: AI PC demand in China and US a positive read-through alongside AAPL per Citi survey
bullets.body: Citi's consumer electronics survey notes strong interest in AI PCs in China and the US, citing DELL and AAPL as primary beneficiaries among OEMs. No specific PT or rating action.

bullets.title: ORCL: Investing 1.7GW of carbon-free power in Texas to support AI data center expansion
bullets.body: Oracle announced an investment in more than 1.7GW of carbon-free electricity to support AI growth and strengthen the Texas grid, linking data-center expansion with incremental clean-power capacity.

bullets.title: CRDO: Attending JPM OCP 2026 conference Oct 13; market cap ~$28.2B; Jefferies NDR Sept 29
bullets.body: Credo Semiconductor is scheduled for a group meeting at JPM's OCP 2026 conference (Oct 13, San Jose) and a Jefferies-hosted NDR with CEO/CFO on Sept 29 in NYC. Market cap noted at ~$28.2B as of today.

bullets.title: Macro: Fed hike 25bp tomorrow near-certain (94-95%); 10Y at 5%, oil +4.2% — tech/consumer under pressure
bullets.body: Markets closed lower (SPX -0.4%, NDX -0.6%) with WTI crude surging 4.2% to $105.52 on Saudi cargo cancellations and Libya/Russia disruptions, pushing the 10Y yield to 5.002% (post-2007 high). Fed is ~94-95% priced for a 25bp hike tomorrow; JPM's five-scenario framework shows the most likely outcomes as neutral to modestly positive for equities. JPM remains bullish Tech, Semis, and Mag7 into the print.
